Diogenes Laërtius, The Lives and Opinions of Eminent Philosophers, translated by C. D. Yonge.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/diogenes-laertius/the-lives-and-opinions-of-eminent-philosophers/c-d-yonge

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Diogenes Laërtius, the author, wrote in the third century AD (SE colophon). Wikidata Q59138 gives his death year as 240.
- C. D. Yonge, the translator, died 1891 (Wikidata Q4205941, P570 = 1891-11-30). He is the last person to die.

First publication of the text used: 1853 (SE colophon: 'The Lives and Opinions of Eminent Philosophers was written in the third century AD by Diogenes Laërtius. It was translated from Greek in 1853 by C. D. Yonge.'). The Wikipedia article on Diogenes Laërtius lists the Yonge translation as published in London by G. H. Bohn in 1853.

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the work was first published in 1853, so it entered the United States public domain 95 years later, in 1948.
- Country of origin (United Kingdom, first publication 1853 in London): copyright there lasts for life plus 70 years after the death of the last person named above. The translator died in 1891, so the translation entered the public domain there on 1 January 1962.
- The Greek original, written in the third century AD according to the colophon, is far older than any copyright term, so no country's copyright still applies to it.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
